reason: The trigger is a native <button type="button"> carrying aria-expanded and an aria-controls naming the region it shows and hides; the region is always rendered, so aria-controls never points at nothing, and it is hidden by the `hidden` attribute alone -- the Tailwind preflight's [hidden] { display: none !important } outranks the region slot's flex, so nothing has to hide it a second time. WHAT IS DELIBERATELY NOT CLAIMED IS TREEVIEW: with arbitrary nesting the rendered structure resembles one, and APG's treeview would demand aria-level on every node, a roving tab stop and four-direction arrow navigation. None of that is designed here and none of it is bound -- each collapsible is an independent disclosure, which is what a nav landmark full of links actually is, and the cost is the one the disclosure pattern's own description states. On the two keyboard requirements this trigger intercepts Enter and Space and preventDefault()s them rather than leaving them to the platform, because the same interception is what stops arena-menu opening twice in a browser and the family is better served by one rule than by two. The behaviour a user meets is the platform's; what differs is who implements it, and the compliance suite measures the interception rather than assuming it.
